A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLIP-powered data-selection framework. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. v1 ends with references; v2 additionally contains Appendices A–M, which were included in the comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments, cross-architecture evaluations, noise robustness tests, timing comparisons, and component ablations in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds CIFAR-10 comparisons, text-modality and threshold experiments, timing measurements, and selection-count analyses.

M1.justification: The CLIP encoders, adapters, semantic-alignment and diversity scores, and selection objective in Equations 1–6 remain unchanged. Appendix B supplies pseudocode for the existing procedure; the image-prototype variant is an experimental control.

E1.justification: Table 10 extends label-noise testing from the existing 20% condition to 50% and 70% noise. The underlying classification datasets remain unchanged. CIFAR-10 was already used in v1; its added accuracy tables do not introduce a new dataset or task.

E2.justification: Section 4.5 and Table 10 add an average-image-feature prototype comparator against the text-based method. The ten main baselines remain unchanged, including in corresponding retained comparisons. Newly cited TDDS and NGC are not reported as additional evaluated algorithms.

E3.justification: The reported adapter-training budget changes from 25 epochs in v1 Section 4.5 to 30 in v2 Appendix C, without establishing which experiments were rerun. Added evaluations use ViT-small and a tighter threshold of 5e-5. Most other newly listed training settings are disclosures rather than demonstrated protocol changes.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained adapter and loss ablations, v2 adds a direct test of text versus image prototypes, threshold sensitivity, and checks of actual versus requested selection counts. Appendices H–M also add noisy-selection visualization and detailed cost analyses, substantially extending the diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations. Appendix C newly specifies three runs with different seeds, except one run per ImageNet-1k case; Appendix I reports averaging timing over five independent runs. These disclosures do not establish increased replication of retained experiments.

E6.justification: Tables 6–11 and Figure 10 add substantial accuracy, timing, threshold, modality-control, and selection-count results. Table 2 revises the method's CIFAR-100 accuracies from 45.63/58.65 to 46.05/58.34 and Tiny-ImageNet accuracies from 25.98/32.21 to 26.09/33.13 at 20%/30% selection. Selected-noise proportions change from 0.24/0.25 to 0.25/0.32. Baseline values and most other main results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds a short mathematical argument and Equation 7 relating the stopping threshold to selection-ratio error, with a sample-count example. v1 states the numerical tolerance without this argument. Existing score definitions, losses, and complexity claims remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and concluding claims retain the same scope: multimodal selection improves robustness, generalization, and efficiency through three modules. Additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds specific limitations concerning inherited CLIP biases and modality imbalance, replacing the brief future-work statement about multimodal datasets and object detection. Appendices J and M add interpretations concerning repeated-model training savings and why selection-count deviations do not explain performance gains.

D1.justification: Appendices B, C, E, F, and I substantially expand reproducibility information through pseudocode, optimizer settings, learning-rate schedules, batch sizes, training budgets, pretrained-model fine-tuning details, implementation sources, and timing hardware. The abstract replaces promised future code release with a repository location and a statement of availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds references covering TDDS, submodular information measures, CLIP bias, noisy-label detection, NGC, and EntAugment, and removes Zhao and Bilen's dataset-condensation citation. The overall positioning as multimodal static data selection remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most main-text wording and section order are retained. Changes include localized editing, publication and author-footnote updates, moving the dataset/architecture description into Appendix C, appendix cross-references, and expanding Section 5 into Discussion and Conclusion.

P2.justification: v2 adds six appendix tables, Figures 8–10, and Algorithm 1. It also merges v1 Tables 2 and 3 into a consolidated noisy-label table, relocates several existing displays, and adjusts framework-diagram labels. These constitute substantial display additions beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: The implementation and replication details, direct text-modality control, and selection-count checks improve reproducibility and the assessment of central claims. Reporting inconsistencies temper these gains: Section 4.5 gives 16.39% as image-prototype accuracy, whereas Table 10 lists 28.42% accuracy and 16.39% noise proportion. Revised Table 2 values also leave the introduction's quoted performance margins unreconciled.
